cases.rendered:
Where the taxable person has given notice of an objection or appeal, collection of tax remains in abeyance until the objection or appeal is determined, subject to section 11 of the Act. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 49(1) to (6)]

The taxable person shall pay the tax which is not the subject of an objection or appeal. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 49(1) to (6)]

Tax charged by an assessment that is not the subject of an objection or appeal is payable within 30 days of service of the notice of assessment, and the relevant tax authority may, in its discretion, extend the time for payment. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 49(1) to (6)]

Once an objection or appeal is determined, the relevant tax authority serves a notice of the tax payable as determined, and that tax is payable within 30 days of the date of service of that notice. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 49(1) to (6)]

Any balance of tax unpaid as at the due date attracts interest and penalties as provided in the Act or any other relevant law. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 49(1) to (6)]

The relevant tax authority shall respond to an objection notice within 90 days, otherwise the objection of the taxpayer shall be upheld. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 41(5) to (8)]

Not covered by the retrieved provisions:
- Section 11 of the Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, which section 49 refers to, is not among the passages.
- The passages do not say how interest or penalties apply to the disputed tax after an objection is decided.

Sources
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 49(1) to (6) (gazette pages A 288, A 289)
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 41(5) to (8) (gazette page A 285)

Differences between official texts
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 41(5) to (8): The Gombe print requires a taxpayer appealing from the Tax Appeal Tribunal to the High Court to pay 20% of the disputed amount first; the cited print has no deposit clause, and Gombe's (9) is its (8). (DR-229)
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 41(5) to (8): The cited print's s41(8) provides appeals from the High Court to the Court of Appeal and then the Supreme Court; the National Assembly text has no such subsection. (DR-231)
